title: Adaptive redispatch policy for geo-capacity-aware request routing
creator: Lucas Meyer
description: Design and implement a dynamic redispatch policy that combines latency-based routing, soft geo-pinning, and capacity-aware steering to preserve SLOs during region degradation. The policy should: 1) prefer low-latency region candidates but respect explicit geo-pins; 2) detect regional capacity stress and redistribute traffic with backoff and decay; 3) integrate with circuit breakers and prioritized load-shedding; 4) be configurable per-customer and per-route; 5) provide observability and safe rollout controls.
acceptance_criteria: Traffic redistributed from a stressed region to healthy regions with >90% of rerouted requests meeting 95th latency SLO compared to baseline within 3 minutes of detection
Circuit breaker trips prevent >99% of requests to severely degraded backends within 30s of threshold breach
Soft geo-pinning honors customer pin preferences for >=95% of pinned requests unless override policies (capacity emergency/circuit-break) apply
Load-shedding preserves high-priority request classes (internal control plane, admin, realtime tokens) while shedding low-priority batch/async requests
Config knobs (latency_threshold_ms, capacity_headroom_pct, pin_ttl_minutes, failover_weight_decay) available in console and as API params
End-to-end e2e test harness simulates multi-region capacity loss and validates fallback behavior in staging
Observability: per-request routing decision tag present in spans and logs, dashboard shows re-dispatch counts, avg latency pre/post redispatch, and percent of pinned overrides
design_decisions: Use a two-tier scoring function: primary=latency SLO delta, secondary=available_tpu/gpu_capacity_headroom to pick destination regions
Implement 'soft-pin' semantics: pins are honored by default but will be overridden when destination headroom < configured emergency threshold; override requires audit log
Prefer gradual redispatch (weighted steering) over binary cutovers to avoid cache stampedes; weights decay over time toward baseline routing
Circuit breaker thresholds are per-region and per-model-profile to account for differing token costs and latency characteristics
Load-shedding prioritizes by request class and token estimate, using a token-bucket style limiter integrated into gateway ingress
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Simulation and scoring model (2 weeks) - build traffic simulator using historic traces, implement scoring heuristic, evaluate trade-offs
Phase 2: Control-plane + policy schema (1 week) - add policy fields to routing config, console UI mocks for knobs
Phase 3: Runtime redispatch + weight decay (3 weeks) - implement in request router, integrate with serving runtime metrics API
Phase 4: Circuit breakers + shedding integration (2 weeks) - hook breakers to router decisions and add prioritized shedding logic
Phase 5: Observability + tests (2 weeks) - tag traces, add dashboards, run chaos/stress tests in staging
Phase 6: Gradual rollout (4 weeks) - opt-in beta customers, k-v feature flag, monitoring alarms and rollback playbook
config_parameters: latency_threshold_ms: 95th percentile latency delta tolerated before considering failover (default 120)
capacity_headroom_pct: minimum free capacity in candidate region to accept additional load (default 20)
pin_ttl_minutes: duration to respect a geo-pin before re-evaluating (default 60)
emergency_override_headroom_pct: headroom below which soft-pins can be force-overridden (default 5)
failover_weight_decay_minutes: how quickly routing weights decay back to baseline after emergency (default 30)
circuit_breaker_rps_threshold: per-region request RPS threshold to trigger breaker (varies by model profile)
shedding_priority_bands: mapping of request classes to shedding priority (control, realtime, interactive, batch)
max_redispatch_fraction: cap of total regional traffic that can be redirected at once (default 0.35)
probe_interval_seconds: how frequently to poll region capacity and latency signals (default 10)
grace_window_seconds: minimum evaluation window before taking aggressive actions (default 60)
audit_log_on_override: boolean flag to record pin overrides for compliance (default true)
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring function and weight calculations
Integration test: run simulated RPS spike in region-A and assert weighted redistribution meets latency SLO in staging
Chaos test: cut network to region-B and validate circuit breaker + shedding prevent noisy neighbor failures
Canary rollout: enable for 5% traffic for internal customers, validate metrics for 48h before increasing
Performance test: ensure routing decision latency added by redispatch logic < 1ms p50 and <5ms p99
Security test: validate audit logs and RBAC for config edits to routing policies
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: redispatch rate, redispatch latency impact (p50/p95/p99), pin-override events, circuit-breaker trips by region
Alert: redispatch_rate > 10% sustained for 5m -> page SRE
Alert: percent_pinned_overridden > 5% in last 15m -> notify product and legal for potential customer impact
Alert: circuit_breaker_trip_rate high or repeated trips within 1h -> page oncall
SLO burn: automatically open incident when 95th latency SLO for customer routes degrades by >10% for 15m
rollout_and_fallback: Start with non-critical routes and internal customers using feature flag
Observe for 48h then expand to low-latency tier customers
Fallback: if redispatch causes SLO regressions, activate 'pin-priority' mode which temporarily disables pin overrides and relies on capacity shedding
Manual rollback: feature flag off will instantly stop redispatch but respects currently in-flight requests; playbook prepared for safe draining
Postmortem runbook linked in linked_artifacts for escalation steps
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: cache stampede due to sudden redirecting of many requests -> Mitigation: weighted redistribution + gradual ramp and cache-warm probes
Risk: violating compliance geo-pins for regulated customers -> Mitigation: soft-pin with strict override audit and customer-level opt-out flag
Risk: oscillation between regions causing increased latency -> Mitigation: add hysteresis and failover_weight_decay to dampen oscillations
Risk: misconfiguration leads to mass-shedding -> Mitigation: conservative defaults, feature flag, and simulated dry-run mode
